title: Collaborative Filtering Meets Spectrum Shift: Connecting User-Item Interaction with Graph-Structured Side Information

problem.claim: Integrating graph-structured side information into the user-item interaction graph can reduce the performance of existing graph collaborative filtering methods.

gap.claim: Existing approaches built for the full spectrum [-1, 1] assign mismatched importance to frequencies after side information shifts the augmented graph spectrum.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes Spectrum Shift Correction (SSC), which uses shifting and scaling factors to adapt spectral graph neural networks to the shifted spectrum.
SSC connects traditional graph collaborative filtering with graph-structured side information without requiring data-type-specific designs.
The paper analyzes the effect of incorporating graph-structured side information from a spectral perspective.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on social and multimodal recommendation reportedly show relative improvements of up to 23% with SSC.
The authors report that SSC achieves these improvements without additional computational overhead.
The authors report that implementation code is available in a public repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph neural networks are effective for collaborative filtering based on user-item interaction graphs.
Adding graph-structured side information causes existing graph collaborative filtering methods to underperform.
The paper attributes the issue to a rightward shift in the highest frequencies of the augmented adjacency spectrum, causing frequency-importance mismatch.
The authors introduce SSC with shifting and scaling factors and position it as a general connection between collaborative filtering and graph-structured side information.
Experiments on social and multimodal recommendation reportedly show improvements of up to 23% without additional computational overhead.

source_observation.claim: Adding graph-structured side information progressively shifts the augmented adjacency spectrum rightward.

interpretation.claim: When data integration changes the operating distribution of graph frequencies, a model designed for the original spectrum may misallocate frequency importance.

application.claim: For graph-based systems that combine interaction data with side information, inspect spectral or distributional shifts and consider explicit correction factors.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether spectrum correction is necessary or beneficial for graph data outside the reported recommendation settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or statistical protocol.
The abstract does not provide the exact shifting and scaling formulations or implementation details.
The abstract does not quantify computational cost or define the comparison used for the no-overhead claim.
